analysis:
This batch contains only documentation. It adds changelog.d/ssd-maintenance-header-verdicts.md (head lines 1-9) and changes one row of docs/reference/ssd-kv-cache.md: the maintenance-sweep row at base/head line 372. The docs say SSDWholeRootMaintainer now also runs after each write job. They also say it caches readable DBK3 header verdicts keyed by lstat identity (device, inode, size, mtime, ctime). It re-parses only new, changed or unreadable files, revalidates fanout directory checks once per pass (fanoutPassesReadChecks), and never caches failed reads. The documented claim is that TTL, budget and ownership decisions are unchanged. This relates to T-041's mitigation (b): TTL expiry, LRU budget and the sweep. Encryption, HMAC naming, AAD, salt scoping and the KEK purge are untouched.

No Swift source for SSDWholeRootMaintainer.swift (readableHeaderIdentities, fanoutPassesReadChecks) or SSDPrefixCacheFactory.swift was supplied. So I cannot verify the following implementation questions:
(1) Whether a remembered header verdict could keep treating a replaced file as owned. The documented ctime/inode keying makes same-identity substitution hard; a same-UID operator (ADV-001) could only affect their own cache availability.
(2) Whether cached verdicts are evicted when files disappear, so the cache does not grow unbounded.
(3) Whether cached TTL/mtime data could delay expiry. The docs say a hit's touch changes mtime and forces a re-parse; TTL should use current lstat times, not the cached header.
(4) Whether running the sweep after every write adds contention with the per-file removal lock or the epoch reread.

The documentation itself does not add attack surface or invalidate a threat assumption. The threat model T-041 detection_hint does not require an update for a read-only header-parse cache, as long as the TTL semantics hold. The integration pass should examine the maintainer source if it is available.
